title: Diffusion Models for High-Dimensional Clustered Data: Intrinsic-Dimension Adaptivity via Bayesian Classification
abstract: arXiv:2608.19067v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The empirical success of diffusion models in generative modelling has motivated theoretical work, including quantitative error bounds and qualitative analyses that characterise the different phases of denoising. We bring these two areas together by studying the adaptivity of diffusion models to the structured geometry of multimodal high-dimensional data that consists of multiple clusters in $\mathbb{R}^D$, each with its own low-dimensional structure, and inter-cluster separation depending on $D$. We employ $K$-mixture Gaussian distributions as a canonical framework to capture this geometry and establish two theoretical results. tldr: 本文通过将去噪过程视为动态贝叶斯分类器，证明了扩散模型在高维聚类数据中能自适应于内在低维结构，并在信噪比达到特定阈值时实现聚类后验概率的集中。
en_tdlr: This paper interprets denoising as a dynamical Bayesian classifier and proves that diffusion models adapt to intrinsic low-dimensional structures in high-dimensional clustered data, with posterior class probabilities concentrating on a single cluster once the signal-to-noise ratio reaches a specific threshold.
